data.title: Praziquantel
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Other antiparasitics_

**Class:** Pyrazinoisoquinoline anthelmintic (anti-trematode, anti-cestode)

## Mechanism of action
- Increases calcium permeability of the worm's tegument → spastic paralysis and tegument damage → exposure to host immunity

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Schistosomiasis (including cercarial dermatitis sequelae and cutaneous schistosomiasis)
- Cysticercosis (cysticercosis cutis, neurocysticercosis — with or after albendazole), taeniasis
- Liver and lung flukes (clonorchiasis, paragonimiasis)

## Dose & formulations
- Schistosomiasis: 40 mg/kg single dose or 20 mg/kg twice in one day
- Taeniasis: 5–10 mg/kg single dose
- Neurocysticercosis: 50 mg/kg/day in 3 doses for 15 days (with steroids)
- Cysticercosis cutis (Khopkar): single or short courses; excision is often curative

## Adverse effects
- Headache, dizziness, abdominal pain, malaise; inflammatory reactions from dying cysts (seizures in neurocysticercosis)

## Contraindications
- Ocular cysticercosis (inflammation can destroy the eye — remove surgically)
- With strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampicin)

## Drug interactions
- Rifampicin, carbamazepine, phenytoin, dexamethasone lower levels; cimetidine raises them

## Pregnancy & lactation
May be used for schistosomiasis in pregnancy (WHO).

## Viva points
- Calcium influx → spastic paralysis of worms
- Never treat ocular cysticercosis medically first

_Sources: Khopkar ch.5 (Table 5.1); Wolverton 4e ch.12. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
